title: Did the population of Ottoman Anatolia collapse in the late sixteenth and seventeenth centuries?
short: Tax surveys show rapid growth in Anatolia to about 1580, but whether the decline that followed was a demographic collapse or an artefact of changing registration remains unsettled.
matters: A large fall in Anatolian population would connect the Celali rebellions, the Little Ice Age droughts of the 1590s, rural flight and the transformation of Ottoman fiscal and military institutions into one crisis comparable to the 'general crisis' of seventeenth-century Europe and China. If the decline was smaller or mainly a shift from registered villages to towns, nomadism and untaxed settlements, then narratives of Ottoman 'decline' and of climate-driven collapse need revision. The question also tests whether Ottoman tax registers can be used for demography at all.
stuck: The detailed provincial surveys (tahrir defterleri) end in most of Anatolia by the 1580s and record taxable household heads rather than people, while the seventeenth-century avarız and cizye registers that follow count fiscal units (avarızhane) whose relation to households changed over time. Comparisons across the two series therefore mix demographic change with changes in what was counted. Most studies cover single districts, the registers are held in two archives with different access regimes, and many have never been transcribed.
solved: A linked village-level dataset across all surviving tahrir and avarız registers for a large sample of Anatolian districts, with a validated model converting each register's fiscal units into households, that produces regional population series from 1520 to 1700 with uncertainty and that agrees with independent evidence such as court records, settlement abandonment and cizye counts.
approach: Agents can help transcribe and structure registers from facsimiles and published editions, match village names across registers and to modern locations, and estimate conversion factors between fiscal units and households where registers overlap.
Regional series could then be tested against climate reconstructions, Celali violence and court-record evidence of flight.

Scaling beyond published registers requires systematic digitization of the Tapu Tahrir (TT.d) and avarız series in the Ottoman Archives in Istanbul and the Kuyûd-ı Kadîme registers in Ankara, with collaboration from archivists and Ottoman palaeographers, since many registers use siyakat numerals and chancery hands that need specialist verification.

existing.title: Essai sur les données statistiques des registres de recensement dans l'Empire ottoman aux XVe et XVIe siècles
existing.venue: Journal of the Economic and Social History of the Orient 1 (1): 9–36
existing.note: Founding statement of the use of tahrir registers for demography, estimating strong sixteenth-century population growth across the empire.

existing.title: Celâlî İsyanları (1550–1603)
existing.note: Linked the Celali rebellions to population growth, landlessness and economic dislocation in Anatolia.

existing.title: Population Pressure in Rural Anatolia, 1450–1600
existing.venue: London: Oxford University Press (London Oriental Series 27)
existing.note: Village-level analysis of tahrir registers arguing that population grew faster than cultivated land in the sixteenth century, producing pressure on resources.

existing.title: Population rise and fall in Anatolia 1550–1620
existing.note: Compared later tahrir registers across districts and identified a turning point from growth to decline around the 1580s.

existing.title: The Great Anatolian Rebellion, 1000–1020/1591–1611
existing.note: Narrative and political history of the Celali uprisings that framed the period as one of rural upheaval.

existing.title: Ottoman census methods in the mid-sixteenth century: three case histories
existing.note: Examined how survey officials actually compiled registers, raising questions about their completeness as counts.

existing.title: Ottoman demographic history (14th–17th centuries): some considerations
existing.venue: Journal of the Economic and Social History of the Orient 35: 187–198
existing.note: Methodological critique of converting tahrir household counts into population estimates.

existing.title: Studies in Defterology
existing.note: Essays on the use of tahrir registers, including their limitations as demographic sources.

existing.title: Ottoman Tax Registers (Tahrir Defterleri)
existing.note: Survey of the registers as quantitative sources for economists and of methods for sampling and analysing them.

existing.title: Population Changes in Ottoman Anatolia during the 16th and 17th Centuries: The 'Demographic Crisis' Reconsidered
existing.venue: International Journal of Middle East Studies 36 (2): 183–205
existing.note: Combined late tahrir and seventeenth-century avarız registers to argue for a severe and lasting decline in rural Anatolian population from the late sixteenth century.

existing.title: The Climate of Rebellion in the Early Modern Ottoman Empire
existing.note: Linked drought and cold in the 1590s, famine, the Celali rebellions and depopulation into a Little Ice Age crisis.

existing.title: The Collapse of Rural Order in Ottoman Anatolia: Amasya 1576–1643
existing.note: Detailed regional study of Amasya documenting rural desertion and the breakdown of the provincial order across the transition from tahrir to avarız registration.

archives.repository: Presidency of the Republic of Türkiye, Directorate of State Archives, Ottoman Archives (BOA), Istanbul
archives.collection: Tapu Tahrir Defterleri (TT.d); avarız and cizye registers in Maliyeden Müdevver (MAD.d) and Kamil Kepeci (KK.d) series
archives.note: Main holdings of fifteenth- and sixteenth-century survey registers and later fiscal registers; the online catalogue lists items and many are viewable as images by registered researchers.

archives.repository: General Directorate of Land Registry and Cadastre (TKGM), Kuyûd-ı Kadîme Archive, Ankara
archives.collection: Detailed (mufassal) tahrir registers, many the final provincial copies of surveys also partly held in Istanbul
archives.note: Access requires permission; the archive's tahrir holdings are essential for districts whose Istanbul copies are lost.

archives.collection: Published facsimile and transcription editions of selected tahrir and muhasebe registers
archives.note: Facsimile editions of selected registers that can serve as training and validation data for transcription.

archives.repository: Türk Tarih Kurumu (Turkish Historical Society), Ankara
archives.collection: Published editions and monographs on individual sancak registers
archives.note: Many district-level transcriptions of tahrir registers, a ready-made corpus for linking villages across registers.

archives.collection: Copies of Ottoman kadı sicilleri (court registers) and bibliographic databases
archives.note: Court registers record flight, abandoned villages and tax disputes, an independent check on register-based population series; holdings for Anatolian courts are uneven.
